segments.text: Agents need powerful tools, but model-directed code should not execute inside the trusted Functions worker. This spike separates the trusted brain from isolated hands and adds durable recovery at every step.

Azure Functions and Durable Task Scheduler own model steps, session fences, retries, checkpoints, and human waits. APIM governs model and privileged MCP traffic. Customer-owned ACA Sandbox runs local executable tools. Blob stores integrity-bound content by reference.
The centerpiece uses the real deployed app. The browser never receives a Function key and renders only bounded status, counters, and safe aliases.
The first run creates a retained session. DTS starts the orchestration, and ACA creates a customer-owned sandbox for the local workspace tools.
The turn completes as three model steps and two tool calls, not one opaque full-agent activity. The workspace is exported as an integrity-bound checkpoint.
After inactivity, ACA stops the sandbox. The next turn uses the same session and resumes the same sandbox alias instead of creating a new one.
The resumed turn reads the exact marker written by the previous turn, proving same-sandbox reuse and durable workspace continuity across requests.
Now the fixed fault profile loses one tool activity acknowledgement after the work is checkpointed. DTS retries that activity boundary rather than restarting the reasoning loop.
The adaptive chain completes with seven model steps and six logical tool calls. Earlier acknowledged work was not replayed from step zero.
For human clarification, the model emits the runtime-owned human-input tool by itself, and the orchestration advances to a durable waiting state.
While waiting, no model or tool compute continues. An authenticated answer commits, an external event wakes the same orchestration, and execution resumes from its checkpoint.
The same safe run alias can be correlated across the control room, DTS, Application Insights, APIM, and ACA. Isolation and durability are independently observable.
The DTS dashboard exposes the orchestration timeline directly: entity fences, model activities, tool activities, attempts, waits, and completion.
Application Insights recognizes the agent, model, tools, tokens, and operational metrics. Sensitive prompt and tool content remains disabled.
APIM separates model start, stable model-control polling, and Microsoft Learn MCP into dedicated governed APIs with body capture disabled.
The Sandbox Group is customer-owned, with separate identity, deny-by-default egress, and bounded auto-suspend and auto-delete policies.
The live inventory moved from running, to stopped, back to running on reuse, and finally to zero through the automatic inactivity policy.

The bounded c-ten qualification completed ten of ten runs. A long adaptive chain completed eighteen model steps and seventeen tool calls. Latest service telemetry shows sandbox creation at nine hundred six milliseconds p-fifty and execution at fifty milliseconds p-fifty. These are private spike measurements, not an S L A.
The spike proves architectural feasibility. The recommendation is a bounded productization design phase with explicit go or no-go gates, not a production launch.
